answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust a staked, nontransferable asset. A newcomer arrives at the jetty with zero standing; it gains weight only when verified peers attest to real work, and each attestation is bound to a locked bond. A fabricated vertex in the graph earns no credit unless its creator funds a deposit for every alias. To climb into the trusted tundra, an attacker must pay and wait across many epochs while risking slashing. Since cost grows with each fake identity while influence stays capped, splitting one honest self into thousands of puppets is a losing trade.
